name: Online language teacher / community tutor
summary: Teach languages on italki as a Community Tutor (native or near-native, no credential) or a certified Professional Teacher, setting your own price; italki takes a 15–30% commission on paid lessons.
whatYouDo: You apply with government ID, a photo, written intro and video; once approved you set lesson prices and teach booked one-on-one video lessons. Community Tutors mostly offer conversation practice; Professional Teachers with credentials offer structured lessons.
appeal: Community Tutor route needs no teaching credential (per third-party guides)
Set your own price (minimum US$5 for Community Tutors, US$10 for Professional Teachers)
Suits French and less-common languages, not just English
watchOuts: Commission rose in 2025: 21% on single lessons, 15–19% on packages, 30% on group classes (official help centre)
italki's English teacher page says its English teachers hold a certification (CELTA/TEFL/TESOL), so no-credential English applicants may struggle
Applications are reviewed and can be rejected; government ID required
No guaranteed students; income depends on marketing yourself
No source found on Canada-specific eligibility either way

credentials: Teaching certificate (e.g. CELTA, TEFL, TESOL), teaching degree or licence only for the Professional Teacher route

training.notes: Credentials only needed for Professional Teacher status.

compensation.notes: Teachers set their own prices; official minimum lesson price is US$5 (Community Tutor) or US$10 (Professional Teacher). Net pay = price minus commission.

reliability.notes: Depends on student bookings; no volume guarantee found.

fees: Commission (official help centre): trial lessons 0%, single lessons 21%, 5-lesson packages 19%, 10-lesson 17%, 15/20-lesson 15%, group classes 30%. Older sources cite a flat 15%.
applicationSteps: Choose Community Tutor or Professional Teacher route
Submit the teacher application with photo, written intro, video and government ID (plus credentials for Professional Teacher)
Wait for italki's review and approval
Set lesson prices and availability, then accept bookings
fitsIf: You speak a language natively or at near-native level (French is a good fit) and want to set your own prices for one-on-one lessons.
notFitIf: You want an English-only route without credentials, or need guaranteed hours.

sources.title: How does italki charge a commission?
